turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I am warning you, Sandip, not out of fear, but out of duty. As a zamindar, it is my responsibility to protect the interests of my people, and I will not stand idly by while you put them at risk.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, Nikhil, always so full of warnings and dire prophecies. Can't you see I'm busy reaping the benefits of my poetry, not worrying about the local Mussulmans?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I warn you, Sandip, the situation is grave. I have received credible information that the local Mussulmans are planning to attack your estate.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, Nikhil, the great seer of troubles, always warning me of this and that. What's the source of this information, the village gossip or the local wise man?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I warn you, Sandip, not out of idle gossip, but because I have received credible reports from trusted sources that the Mussulmans are indeed gathering arms and planning to attack our estates.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, Nikhil, always so ready to spread doom and gloom. I'm sure the world would come to an end without your warnings, but I think I can handle a few angry Mussulmans on my own, don't you?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I assure you, Sandip, that the situation is grave and requires immediate attention. The Mussulmans are growing increasingly restless, and I fear that your...lighthearted approach may only serve to exacerbate the problem.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, Nikhil, always so quick to sound the alarm, aren't you? Tell me, what's the worst that could happen? The Mussulmans might just decide to take over my estate and I'll have to spend the rest of my days doing the haram thing - being a good landlord!

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I warn you, Sandip, for I have seen the signs of unrest among the Mussulmans. Their discontent will not be easily contained, and it is only a matter of time before they strike.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Ah, Nikhil, always the alarmist, I see. The Mussulmans, you say? Ha! I'm more worried about my poetical reputation being ruined by your constant warnings.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I warn you, Sandip, not for the sake of your reputation, but for the safety of your people and your estate. The Mussulmans are not to be trifled with.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, please, Nikhil, spare me the drama. I'm not exactly trembling with fear at the thought of the Mussulmans. What, are they planning to invade my estate with nothing but their prayers and their tea?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I warn you, Sandip, do not underestimate the situation. These are not empty threats, and I have reason to believe the Mussulmans are growing restless.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, spare me the theatrics, Nikhil. I'm shaking in my boots, not. What's really behind these 'restless Mussulmans' of yours?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not be swayed by your sarcasm, Sandip. The situation is grave, and I will not stand idly by while our village is threatened.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh please, Nikhil, you think a few disgruntled Mussulmans can scare me? My village has been 'threatened' by your seriousness for years, and we're still standing.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Nikhilji, perhaps we can discuss the matter further in private, without the need for such dramatic warnings?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not be swayed by your frivolity, Sandip. The security of our lands is not a matter for jest.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Come, Nikhil, let us not pretend that every Mussulman is a bloodthirsty savage. I'm sure they're just as tired of your holier-than-thou attitude as I am.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not engage in petty exchanges with you, Sandip. The safety of my family and my estate is at stake, and I will not be swayed by your flippant attitude.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I say, Nikhil, don't you keep Browning among your books here? I was just telling Queen Bee of our college club. Do you remember that contest of ours over the translation of those lines from Browning? You don't?

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I managed to get together the words to render it into Bengali, somehow, but the result was hardly likely to be a 'joy forever' to the people of Bengal. I really did think at one time that I was on the verge of becoming a poet, but Providence was kind enough to save me from that disaster. Do you remember old Dakshina? If he had not become a Salt Inspector, he would have been a poet. I remember his rendering to this day ...

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: No, Queen Bee, it is no use rummaging those bookshelves. Nikhil has ceased to read poetry since his marriage--perhaps he has no further need for it. But I suppose 'the fever fit of poesy', as the Sanskrit has it, is about to attack me again.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you a warning, Sandip

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: About the fever fit of poesy?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: For some time, Mahomedan preachers have been about stirring up the local Mussulmans. They are all wild with you, and may attack you any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Are you come to advise flight?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you information, not to offer advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Had these estates been mine, such a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for me. If, instead of trying to frighten me, you give them a taste of your intimidation, that would be worthier both of you and me. Do you know that your weakness is weakening your neighbouring zamindars also?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I did not offer you my advice, Sandip. I wish you, too, would refrain from giving me yours. Besides, it is useless. And there is another thing I want to tell you. You and your followers have been secretly worrying and oppressing my tenantry. I cannot allow that any longer. So I must ask you to leave my territory.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: For fear of the Mussulmans, or is there any other fear you have to threaten me with?
